rubrics.criterion: The cgroup-side helper in the cgroup utility layer that resolves a container's effective memory/swap budget no longer exposes each resolved value (RAM limit, RAM usage, memory+swap limit, memory+swap usage) as its own scalar out-parameter in a long adjacent same-type list; the resolved budget - including the swap-accounting availability - is produced and consumed as one record.
rubrics.rationale: This resolver is the point where the budget first became split: the injected refactor moved cgroup-side resolution into one shared helper but returned the budget piecewise. Grading must verify the root of the clump was bundled, not merely that some downstream signature got shorter.

rubrics.criterion: The step that derives the container's swap figures from the resolved budget takes the budget (with its swap-accounting availability) as a bundled input and hands its results (swap total, swap usage, swappiness hint) back as a record rather than through adjacent same-type scalar parameters and out-pointers.
rubrics.rationale: This signature originally consumed the same budget positionally (four by-value scalars plus a flag) and wrote three scalar out-parameters; a repair that bundles at the resolver but still re-splits the budget for this helper has only moved the splitting one hop down the chain.

rubrics.criterion: The shared clamp policy that decides the reported swap pool size receives the memory-limit figure and the derived swap figures without a train of four or more adjacent same-type scalar parameters (in values or out values).
rubrics.rationale: The clamp helper is the third signature carrying the same data positionally (five adjacent by-value scalars plus an out-pointer); the clump is only resolved when all three signature families are bundled.

rubrics.criterion: Both report entry points that print swap numbers - the reader that emits the virtual swap-device row and the reader that rewrites the meminfo fields - were migrated consistently: each obtains the budget through the bundled interface and derives its reported SwapTotal/SwapFree/swap row through the bundled path, rather than keeping a per-field positional unpacking bridge.
rubrics.rationale: The two readers are independent consumers in different files from the resolver; leaving one them still plumbing positionally is the most likely incomplete repair because each reader only breaks the compiler when its own signatures change.

rubrics.criterion: The shared-header declaration that API readers see was migrated together with the implementation: the installed cgroup utility header carries the bundled form of the resolution interface (record type and single-budget-typed declaration), without leaving a second parallel copy of the old parameter list anywhere.
rubrics.rationale: The resolver was exported, so its declaration repeats the clump for every API reader; a header left in the old shape keeps the split contract alive even when all .c sites are fixed.

rubrics.criterion: The layering produced by the earlier consolidation is kept: memory-controller resolution still lives in one shared point in the cgroup utility layer, and swap derivation/clamping still live in the reporting layer; the bundling must not be achieved by duplicating controller-resolution logic back into either reader.
rubrics.rationale: The task constrains the fix to the way data travels, not a rollback of the consolidation; a solver can accidentally 'fix' the clump by re-inlining resolution per reader, which reintroduces the duplication the refactor removed.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor leaves no dead budget plumbing behind: no unused or set-but-never-read scalar locals, unused out-parameters, or fetch-string buffers remain in either report reader or the helpers after the migration (compiler-visible unused variables count as a failure).
rubrics.rationale: The injected readers carried per-field string locals and scalar copies whose only purpose was positionally shuttling budget fields; solvers commonly finish the semantic change but leave these locals in place.

rubrics.criterion: No parallel old-shape remnants exist alongside the bundled interface: no ignored or vestigial scalar parameter left in a migrated signature, no now-unreachable helper variant re-exposing the positional form, and no duplicated contract comment that still describes the per-out-parameter interface.
rubrics.rationale: Half-migrations that keep the old parameters 'for compatibility' inside the library (which has no external consumers of that new helper) preserve the clump's documentation and dead surface without preserving behavior.

rubrics.criterion: Unit-conversion timing is preserved: the meminfo path still converts the RAM limit and usage from bytes to kB only after the swap figures are derived, so MemTotal clamping against the host total, MemFree/MemAvailable arithmetic, and the limit value handed to the swap clamp are all the same numbers as before (no early or double conversion when bundling).
rubrics.rationale: Bundling makes it tempting to normalize units into the record once; moving the kB boundary changes several reported meminfo fields and the clamp input, and compiles fine because all fields are the same type.

rubrics.criterion: Failure semantics are preserved: a failed resolution of the RAM budget still produces the same visible outcome (host-complete meminfo output for that reader, empty swaps listing for the other), and unresolvable memory+swap values still yield a zero swap budget with the swappiness hint left at its default.
rubrics.rationale: The resolver distinguishes fatal RAM failures from tolerated memory+swap failures; a bundled record whose fields silently swallow error paths would change which fallback the reports produce on kernels without swap accounting.

rubrics.criterion: The swap-accounting availability gate still controls whether the swappiness hint is consulted: when the memory+swap budget is unresolvable, the reported totals may not depend on a swappiness read (e.g., a host with a configured swappiness of zero must not start reporting an empty swap pool where it previously reported the clamped pool, and vice versa).
rubrics.rationale: The swap-account flag is the least self-explanatory field of the bundle; dropping or miswrapping it is invisible on v2 hosts and only manifests on swapaccount-off v1 hosts with swappiness tuned to zero.

rubrics.criterion: The clamp policy still produces identical totals in both readers: on the v1 path the reported total still includes the memory+swap-vs-RAM headroom (with each reader passing its own correctly scaled limit), the host swap-device clamp and the zero-swappiness suppression still apply, and no reader regains a private drift of the policy.
rubrics.rationale: Bundling the derived swap figures risks mishandling which limit unit each reader supplies (bytes-derived kB in one path, host-clamped kB in the other); this is the concrete observable regression this instance can suffer while appearing fully bundled.
